_comment: ChatGPT (Developer mode connector) → hosted OmniMind MCP. Steps: ChatGPT → Settings → Connectors → Advanced → enable Developer mode → Create → name OmniMind, URL below. Authentication: when the hosted server runs in OAuth resource-server mode (OMNIMIND_MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER / _JWKS_URL / _AUDIENCE — docs/runbooks/omnimind-mcp.md §9; BoardRoom then shows the OAuth path first), choose OAuth and ChatGPT completes the sign-in flow without a token. Otherwise choose 'Custom header' / API key and paste `Authorization: Bearer omt_…` (token from BoardRoom Settings → Connected AI tools) — header auth is not offered on every workspace or plan, and a workspace that allows only OAuth connectors rejects it. ChatGPT uses the read-only `search` and `fetch` tools (readOnlyHint: true, no confirmation prompt). Revoking the token in Settings cuts access within about a minute. The `_local_http_server` block is the LEGACY single-user path: a self-run HTTP server with one static inbound bearer (OMNIMIND_MCP_API_KEY), the process identity chatgpt-desktop-josh (read-only, sourceWeight 0.6) and that identity's own omk_ key as OMNIMIND_MCP_STATIC_AGENT_KEY; it only works with clients that can send a header, so for ChatGPT itself use the hosted path.

hosted_connector.name: OmniMind
hosted_connector.authentication: OAuth when the server has OMNIMIND_MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER configured (preferred where available); otherwise custom header `Authorization: Bearer omt_…` where the workspace offers it

_health_check: curl -s https://omnimind-mcp-production.up.railway.app/health  (no auth; returns exactly {status, uptime, sessions} — agent/tenant are deliberately not exposed)
